The amount of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$ required to produce $110.0\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{KNO}_{3}$ is

(Given: Atomic masses of $\mathrm{H},\mathrm{O},\mathrm{N}$ and $\mathrm{K}$ are $1,16,14$ and 39, respectively.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} 4\mathrm{HNO}_{3}(\mathrm{l})+3\mathrm{KCl}(\mathrm{s})⟶\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{NOCl}(\mathrm{g})+ \\ 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{KNO}_{3}(\mathrm{s}) \end{array}$

$\because 110\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{KNO}_{3}\Rightarrow$ moles of $\mathrm{KNO}_{3}=\frac{110}{101}$

As, 4 mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$ produces $3\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{KNO}_{3}$. 

Hence, the moles of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$ required to produce

Hence, mass of $\mathrm{HNO}_{3}$ required is $1.452\times 63$

text:
Given below are the quantum numbers for 4 electrons.

A. $\mathrm{n}=3,l=2,\mathrm{m}_{l}=1,\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=+1/2$

B. $\mathrm{n}=4,l=1,\mathrm{m}_{l}=0,\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=+1/2$

C. $\mathrm{n}=4,l=2,\mathrm{m}_{l}=-2,\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=-1/2$

D. $\mathrm{n}=3,l=1,\mathrm{m}_{l}=-1,\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=+1/2$

The correct order of increasing energy is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The order of increasing energy of electrons in an atom can generally be determined using the principal quantum number ($n$) and the azimuthal quantum number ($l$). The energy can be compared using the rule: the higher the $(n+l)$ value, the higher the energy. If two electrons have the same $(n+l)$ value, the electron with the higher $n$ value has the higher energy.

Analyze each electron's quantum numbers:

A. $n=3,l=2\Rightarrow n+l=3+2=5$

B. $n=4,l=1\Rightarrow n+l=4+1=5$

C. $n=4,l=2\Rightarrow n+l=4+2=6$

D. $n=3,l=1\Rightarrow n+l=3+1=4$

Comparing the values of $(n+l)$ and the principal quantum number $n$:

D: $n+l=4$, and $n=3$.

A and B: $n+l=5$, but A has $n=3$ while B has $n=4$. Therefore, A has a slightly lower energy than B.

C: $n+l=6$.

Thus, the correct order of increasing energy is:

$D<A<B<C$

Therefore, Option B is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text: Octahedral complexes of copper(II) undergo structural distortion (Jahn-Teller). Which one of the given copper (II) complexes will show the maximum structural distortion? (en - ethylenediamine; $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{NH}_{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{9}$. In a regular octahedron its configuration $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{3}$ is degenerate, because the odd $e_{g}$ electron can occupy either $d_{z^{2}}$ or $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$; the complex therefore distorts, usually by lengthening the two axial bonds, to remove this degeneracy.

The degeneracy, and with it the Jahn–Teller distortion, is greatest when all six ligands are identical, so that the undistorted complex would be a perfect octahedron: this is $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ in $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$.

In $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en})(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}$ and in cis- and trans-$[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]$ the mixed ligand sets already lower the symmetry below octahedral and partly split the $e_{g}$ level, so the additional Jahn–Teller distortion is smaller.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

solution.body:
In compound A the central carbon carries four groups: $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, H, a (Z)-prop-1-enyl group and an (E)-prop-1-enyl group (both $-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$).

By the CIP rules $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ ranks first, the (Z)-propenyl group ranks above the (E)-propenyl group, and H ranks last. In A, with H on the dashed bond, $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ → Z-propenyl → E-propenyl runs anticlockwise, so A has the S configuration.

In the compound of Statement II the (E)-propenyl group is drawn where the mirror image of A would carry the (Z)-propenyl group, and vice versa. With H on the dashed bond, $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ → Z-propenyl → E-propenyl again runs anticlockwise, so this compound is also S: it is A itself, not its mirror image (the enantiomer of A is R). text: A 1.84 mg sample of polyhydric alcoholic compound 'X' of molar mass 92.0 g/mol gave 1.344 mL of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ gas at STP. The number of alcoholic hydrogens present in compound 'X' is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
STP conditions define the volume of 1 mole of any gas as $22.4$ liters or $22400$ mL. The volume of hydrogen gas evolved here is $1.344$ mL, so we can calculate the number of moles of hydrogen gas ($H_{2}$) using the formula:

$n=\frac{V}{V_{m}}$ 

where:

$n$ is the number of moles,
$V$ is the volume of the gas, and
$V_{m}$ is the molar volume of the gas.

Substituting in the given values:

$n=\frac{1.344\text{mL}}{22400\text{mL/mol}}=6.0\times 10^{-5}\text{mol}$

Each molecule of $H_{2}$ contains $2$ atoms of hydrogen. Therefore, the number of moles of hydrogen atoms is twice the number of moles of hydrogen gas:

$n_{H}=2\times n=2\times 6.0\times 10^{-5}\text{mol}=1.2\times 10^{-4}\text{mol}$

This number of moles of hydrogen represents the number of moles of alcoholic hydrogen atoms in the $1.84$ mg sample of the compound 'X'. 

We can determine the number of moles of compound 'X' in the sample by dividing the mass of the sample by the molar mass of the compound:

$n_{X}=\frac{m}{M}$

where:

$n_{X}$ is the number of moles of 'X',
$m$ is the mass of 'X', and
$M$ is the molar mass of 'X'.

Substituting in the given values:

$n_{X}=\frac{1.84\text{mg}}{92\text{g/mol}}=\frac{1.84\times 10^{-3}\text{g}}{92\text{g/mol}}=2.0\times 10^{-5}\text{mol}$

The number of alcoholic hydrogens per molecule of 'X' is then given by the ratio of the number of moles of hydrogen to the number of moles of 'X':

$\frac{n_{H}}{n_{X}}=\frac{1.2\times 10^{-4}\text{mol}}{2.0\times 10^{-5}\text{mol}}=6$

So, compound 'X' contains $6$ alcoholic hydrogens.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift

text:
The number of stereoisomers formed in a reaction of $(\pm )\mathrm{Ph}(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O})\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CN})\mathrm{Ph}$ with $\mathrm{HCN}$ is $___________$.

[where $\mathrm{Ph}$ is $-\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
HCN adds across the C=O group of the cyanohydrin ketone, so the product is $\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CN})-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CN})-\mathrm{Ph}$.


[IMG]

The product has two stereocentres, each carrying the same set of groups ($\mathrm{Ph}$, $\mathrm{OH}$, $\mathrm{CN}$ and the other half of the molecule), so the two halves of the molecule are identical.

A molecule with two identical stereocentres exists as one pair of enantiomers, (R,R) and (S,S), and one optically inactive meso form, (R,S), which has an internal plane of symmetry.

Number of stereoisomers $=2+1=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 29th July Evening Shift
